body.en: Functions, their inverses, and transcendental transformations account for approximately 20% of the EST II Math Level 1 exam. Mastery requires evaluating and restricting composite functions, constructing algebraic inverses, analyzing natural and base-\(b\) logarithms, applying rational function asymptote theorems, and mapping geometric transformations across parent functions.

label.en: Definition 2.1 — Function Composition, Invertibility, and Logarithmic Relations
label.ar: تعريف 2.1 — الدالة Composition, Invertibility, and Logarithmic Relations

body.en:
Core structural definitions of functions and inverse mappings:
  • Function Composition: The composition \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\) applies \(g\) first, then applies \(f\) to the output. The domain of \(f \circ g\) is:
    \[ \text{Dom}(f \circ g) = \{ x \in \text{Dom}(g) \mid g(x) \in \text{Dom}(f) \} \]
  • Inverse Functions & Invertibility Criterion: A function \(f\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}\) if and only if it is one-to-one (injective), passing the Horizontal Line Test:
    \[ f(a) = f(b) \implies a = b \]
    The fundamental cancellation identity states:
    \[ (f \circ f^{-1})(x) = x \quad \text{and} \quad (f^{-1} \circ f)(x) = x \]
    The graph of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) is the reflection of \(y = f(x)\) across the line \(y = x\).
  • Logarithmic Foundation: The logarithmic function with base \(b > 0, b \neq 1\) is the exact inverse of the exponential function \(y = b^x\):
    \[ y = \log_b(x) \iff b^y = x \quad (x > 0) \]
    The natural logarithm uses base \(e\): \(\ln(x) = \log_e(x)\).
body.ar:
Core structural definitions of الدوال and inverse mappings:
  • Function Composition: The composition \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\) applies \(g\) first, then applies \(f\) to the output. The المجال of \(f \circ g\) is:
    \[ \text{Dom}(f \circ g) = \{ x \in \text{Dom}(g) \mid g(x) \in \text{Dom}(f) \} \]
  • Inverse الدوال & Invertibility Criterion: A الدالة \(f\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}\) if and only if it is one-to-one (injective), passing the Horizontal Line Test:
    \[ f(a) = f(b) \implies a = b \]
    The fundamental cancellation المتطابقة states:
    \[ (f \circ f^{-1})(x) = x \quad \text{and} \quad (f^{-1} \circ f)(x) = x \]
    The التمثيل البياني of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) is the reflection of \(y = f(x)\) across the line \(y = x\).
  • Logarithmic Foundation: The logarithmic الدالة with base \(b > 0, b \neq 1\) is the exact inverse of the exponential الدالة \(y = b^x\):
    \[ y = \log_b(x) \iff b^y = x \quad (x > 0) \]
    The natural logarithm uses base \(e\): \(\ln(x) = \log_e(x)\).

label.ar: ● الحدس المفاهيمي العميق — الدوال: Composite, Inverse & Logarithmic

body.en: Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental function \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical equations, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the solution set, requiring a final domain check against the original equation.
body.ar: Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental الدالة \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical المعادلات, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the الحل set, requiring a final المجال check against the original المعادلة.

label.en: Theorem 2.1 — Logarithmic Laws, Change of Base, and Rational Function Asymptotes
label.ar: مبرهنة 2.1 — Logarithmic Laws, Change of Base, and Rational الدالة خطوط التقارب

body.en:
Analytical laws governing functional calculations and asymptotic structures:
  • Operational Laws of Logarithms (for \(x, y > 0\)):
    1. Product: \(\log_b(xy) = \log_b x + \log_b y\)
    2. Quotient: \(\log_b\left(\frac{x}{y}\right) = \log_b x - \log_b y\)
    3. Power: \(\log_b(x^p) = p \log_b x\)
    4. Change of Base Formula: For any valid base \(c\):
    \[ \log_b a = \frac{\log_c a}{\log_c b} = \frac{\ln a}{\ln b} = \frac{\log_{10} a}{\log_{10} b} \]
  • Rational Function Asymptotes: For \(f(x) = \frac{a_n x^n + \dots + a_0}{b_m x^m + \dots + b_0}\):
    1. Vertical Asymptote: Occurs at real zeros of the denominator that are not roots of the numerator.
    2. Horizontal Asymptote:
    • If \(n < m\): Horizontal asymptote at \(y = 0\).
    • If \(n = m\): Horizontal asymptote at \(y = \frac{a_n}{b_m}\) (ratio of leading coefficients).
    • If \(n > m\): No horizontal asymptote (if \(n = m + 1\), an oblique slant asymptote \(y = mx + b\) is found via polynomial division).

label.en: ▲ EST II Math Traps & Pitfalls — Composite, Inverse & Logarithmic Functions
label.ar: ▲ EST II Math Traps & Pitfalls — Composite, Inverse & Logarithmic الدوال

body.en:
• Domain of Composite Functions: For \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\), \(x\) must reside in the domain of \(g\) AND \(g(x)\) must fall within the domain of \(f\). Never simplify algebraically before checking initial domain constraints.
  • Inverse Functions and One-to-One: \(f^{-1}(x)\) exists only if \(f\) passes the Horizontal Line Test. When swapping \(x\) and \(y\), remember that the range of \(f\) becomes the domain of \(f^{-1}\). For restricted domains like \(f(x) = x^2, x \ge 0\), the inverse is \(f^{-1}(x) = \sqrt{x}, x \ge 0\).
  • Logarithm Laws vs. False Analogies: \(\log(a + b) \neq \log a + \log b\). Only multiplication inside yields addition outside: \(\log(ab) = \log a + \log b\). Similarly, \(\frac{\log a}{\log b} \neq \log(a - b)\) — it is the change-of-base formula \(\log_b a\).
  • Function Transformations Order: For \(y = a f(b(x - c)) + d\), horizontal stretch/compression by \(1/|b|\) and shift by \(c\) occur inside, while vertical stretch by \(a\) and vertical shift by \(d\) occur outside. \(f(x - c)\) shifts right by \(c\); \(f(x + c)\) shifts left.
body.ar:
• Domain of Composite الدوال: For \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\), \(x\) must reside in the المجال of \(g\) AND \(g(x)\) must fall within the المجال of \(f\). Never بسّط algebraically before checking initial المجال constraints.
  • Inverse الدوال and One-to-One: \(f^{-1}(x)\) exists only if \(f\) passes the Horizontal Line Test. عندما swapping \(x\) and \(y\), remember that the المدى of \(f\) becomes the المجال of \(f^{-1}\). For restricted domains like \(f(x) = x^2, x \ge 0\), the inverse is \(f^{-1}(x) = \sqrt{x}, x \ge 0\).
  • Logarithm Laws vs. False Analogies: \(\log(a + b) \neq \log a + \log b\). Only multiplication inside yields addition outside: \(\log(ab) = \log a + \log b\). Similarly, \(\frac{\log a}{\log b} \neq \log(a - b)\) — it is the change-of-base الصيغة \(\log_b a\).
  • Function Transformations Order: For \(y = a f(b(x - c)) + d\), horizontal stretch/compression by \(1/|b|\) and shift by \(c\) occur inside, while vertical stretch by \(a\) and vertical shift by \(d\) occur outside. \(f(x - c)\) shifts right by \(c\); \(f(x + c)\) shifts left.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Functions: Composite, Inverse & Logarithmic)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (الدوال: Composite, Inverse & Logarithmic)

body.en:
Why Completing the Square & Log-Linearization Work: Any quadratic \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \ne 0\)) can be rewritten by factoring \(a\) from the first two terms and adding/subtracting \((b/2a)^2\):

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the range to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

label.en: Worked Example 2.A — Algebraic Inversion of Rational Functions
label.ar: مثال محلول 2.A — Algebraic Inversion of Rational الدوال

body.en:
Let \(f(x) = \dfrac{3x - 4}{2x + 5}\) for \(x eq - rac{5}{2}\).
(a) Find the inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\).
(b) Determine the domain and range of \(f^{-1}(x)\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Construct \(f^{-1}(x)\):
    Set \(y = rac{3x - 4}{2x + 5}\) and swap variables \(x\) and \(y\):
    \[ x = rac{3y - 4}{2y + 5} \]
    Cross-multiply:
    \[ x(2y + 5) = 3y - 4 \implies 2xy + 5x = 3y - 4 \]
    Isolate terms with \(y\):
    \[ 2xy - 3y = -5x - 4 \implies y(2x - 3) = -(5x + 4) \implies y = rac{-(5x + 4)}{2x - 3} = rac{5x + 4}{3 - 2x} \]
    Thus, \(\mathbf{f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{5x + 4}{3 - 2x} = -\dfrac{5x + 4}{2x - 3}}\).
  2. (b) Domain and Range:
    The denominator of \(f^{-1}\) cannot vanish: \(3 - 2x eq 0 \implies x eq rac{3}{2}\).
    Domain of \(f^{-1}\): \(\mathbf{\left(-\infty, rac{3}{2} ight) \cup \left( rac{3}{2}, \infty ight)}\).
    The range of \(f^{-1}\) is the domain of \(f\): \(\mathbf{\left(-\infty, - rac{5}{2} ight) \cup \left(- rac{5}{2}, \infty ight)}\).
body.ar:
Let \(f(x) = \dfrac{3x - 4}{2x + 5}\) for \(x eq - rac{5}{2}\).
(a) أوجد inverse الدالة \(f^{-1}(x)\).
(b) حدّد المجال and المدى of \(f^{-1}(x)\).

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. (a) Construct \(f^{-1}(x)\):
    Set \(y = rac{3x - 4}{2x + 5}\) and swap المتغيرات \(x\) and \(y\):
    \[ x = rac{3y - 4}{2y + 5} \]
    Cross-multiply:
    \[ x(2y + 5) = 3y - 4 \implies 2xy + 5x = 3y - 4 \]
    Isolate terms with \(y\):
    \[ 2xy - 3y = -5x - 4 \implies y(2x - 3) = -(5x + 4) \implies y = rac{-(5x + 4)}{2x - 3} = rac{5x + 4}{3 - 2x} \]
    Thus, \(\mathbf{f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{5x + 4}{3 - 2x} = -\dfrac{5x + 4}{2x - 3}}\).
  2. (b) المجال and المدى:
    The denominator of \(f^{-1}\) cannot vanish: \(3 - 2x eq 0 \implies x eq rac{3}{2}\).
    Domain of \(f^{-1}\): \(\mathbf{\left(-\infty, rac{3}{2} ight) \cup \left( rac{3}{2}, \infty ight)}\).
    The المدى of \(f^{-1}\) is the المجال of \(f\): \(\mathbf{\left(-\infty, - rac{5}{2} ight) \cup \left(- rac{5}{2}, \infty ight)}\).

label.en: Worked Example 2.B — Solving Logarithmic Equations with Base Differences
label.ar: مثال محلول 2.B — Solving Logarithmic المعادلات with Base Differences

body.en:
Solve the equation \(\log_2(x) + \log_4(x) = 6\) for \(x\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Apply Change of Base to \(\log_4(x)\):
    Express \(\log_4(x)\) in base 2:
    \[ \log_4(x) = \frac{\log_2(x)}{\log_2(4)} = \frac{\log_2(x)}{2} = \frac{1}{2} \log_2(x) \]
  2. Substitute into the equation:
    \[ \log_2(x) + \frac{1}{2} \log_2(x) = 6 \implies \frac{3}{2} \log_2(x) = 6 \]
  3. Multiply by \(\frac{2}{3}\):
    \[ \log_2(x) = 6 \times \frac{2}{3} = 4 \]
  4. Convert to exponential form:
    \[ x = 2^4 = \mathbf{16} \]
  5. Check validity: \(x = 16 > 0\) satisfies all initial arguments: \(\log_2(16) + \log_4(16) = 4 + 2 = 6\) ✓.
The solution is \(\mathbf{x = 16}\).
body.ar:
حل المعادلة \(\log_2(x) + \log_4(x) = 6\) for \(x\).

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. Apply Change of Base to \(\log_4(x)\):
    Express \(\log_4(x)\) in base 2:
    \[ \log_4(x) = \frac{\log_2(x)}{\log_2(4)} = \frac{\log_2(x)}{2} = \frac{1}{2} \log_2(x) \]
  2. Substitute into the المعادلة:
    \[ \log_2(x) + \frac{1}{2} \log_2(x) = 6 \implies \frac{3}{2} \log_2(x) = 6 \]
  3. Multiply by \(\frac{2}{3}\):
    \[ \log_2(x) = 6 \times \frac{2}{3} = 4 \]
  4. Convert to exponential form:
    \[ x = 2^4 = \mathbf{16} \]
  5. Check validity: \(x = 16 > 0\) satisfies all initial arguments: \(\log_2(16) + \log_4(16) = 4 + 2 = 6\) ✓.
The الحل is \(\mathbf{x = 16}\).

label.en: Worked Example 2.C — Composite Function Domain Restriction
label.ar: مثال محلول 2.C — Composite الدالة المجال Restriction

body.en:
Let \(f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x - 3}\) and \(g(x) = \sqrt{x + 2}\). Determine the exact domain of the composite function \((f \circ g)(x)\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Step 1: Domain of the inner function \(g(x)\):
    The radicand must be non-negative: \[ x + 2 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -2 \]
  2. Step 2: Restrict outputs of \(g(x)\) from the domain of \(f\):
    The function \(f(u) = rac{1}{u - 3}\) is defined for \(u eq 3\).
    Therefore, \(g(x) eq 3\):
    \[ \sqrt{x + 2} eq 3 \implies x + 2 eq 9 \implies x eq 7 \]
  3. Step 3: Intersect the conditions:
    Combining \(x \ge -2\) and \(x eq 7\) gives in interval notation:
    \[ \mathbf{[-2, 7) \cup (7, \infty)} \]
body.ar:
Let \(f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x - 3}\) and \(g(x) = \sqrt{x + 2}\). حدّد exact المجال of the composite الدالة \((f \circ g)(x)\).

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. Step 1: المجال of the inner الدالة \(g(x)\):
    The radicand must be non-negative: \[ x + 2 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -2 \]
  2. Step 2: Restrict outputs of \(g(x)\) from the المجال of \(f\):
    The الدالة \(f(u) = rac{1}{u - 3}\) is defined for \(u eq 3\).
    Therefore, \(g(x) eq 3\):
    \[ \sqrt{x + 2} eq 3 \implies x + 2 eq 9 \implies x eq 7 \]
  3. Step 3: Intersect the conditions:
    Combining \(x \ge -2\) and \(x eq 7\) gives in interval notation:
    \[ \mathbf{[-2, 7) \cup (7, \infty)} \]

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Functions: Composite, Inverse & Logarithmic (Easy Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(D\) — الدوال: Composite, Inverse & Logarithmic (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): Given the function \( f(x) = 2x + 3 \). What is the value of \( f^{-1}(7) \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: Let \( y = f(x) \). Then \( y = 2x + 3 \). To find the inverse function \( f^{-1}(y) \), we swap \( x \) and \( y \) and solve for \( y \). So, \( x = 2y + 3 \). Subtract 3 from both sides: \( x - 3 = 2y \). Divide by 2: \( y = \frac{x - 3}{2} \). Thus, \( f^{-1}(x) = \frac{x - 3}{2} \). We need to find \( f^{-1}(7) \). Substitute \( x = 7 \) into the inverse function: \( f^{-1}(7) = \frac{7 - 3}{2} = \frac{4}{2} = 2 \).
body.ar:
Problem (Easy): المعطيات the الدالة \( f(x) = 2x + 3 \). What is the value of \( f^{-1}(7) \)?

Step-by-Step الحل: Let \( y = f(x) \). Then \( y = 2x + 3 \). To أوجد inverse الدالة \( f^{-1}(y) \), we swap \( x \) and \( y \) and أوجد قيمة \( y \). So, \( x = 2y + 3 \). Subtract 3 from both sides: \( x - 3 = 2y \). Divide by 2: \( y = \frac{x - 3}{2} \). وعليه, \( f^{-1}(x) = \frac{x - 3}{2} \). We need to find \( f^{-1}(7) \). عوّض \( x = 7 \) into the inverse الدالة: \( f^{-1}(7) = \frac{7 - 3}{2} = \frac{4}{2} = 2 \).

question.en: Given \(f(x) = e^x\) and \(g(x) = \ln(x + 1)\), find the domain of \((g \circ f)(x)\) and evaluate \((g \circ f)(0)\).
question.ar: Given \(f(x) = e^x\) and \(g(x) = \ln(x + 1)\), أوجد مجال \((g \circ f)(x)\) and احسب قيمة \((g \circ f)(0)\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Formulate composite function: \[ (g \circ f)(x) = g(f(x)) = \ln(e^x + 1). \]

Step 2: Analyze domain requirements: The argument of the natural log must be strictly positive: \[ e^x + 1 > 0. \] Since \(e^x > 0\) for all real numbers \(x\), \(e^x + 1 > 1 > 0\) holds universally. The domain is all real numbers: \(\mathbf{(-\infty, \infty)}\).

Step 3: Evaluate at \(x = 0\): \[ (g \circ f)(0) = \ln(e^0 + 1) = \ln(1 + 1) = \mathbf{\ln(2)} \approx 0.693. \]

question.en: Let \(f(x) = \dfrac{2x + 1}{x - 3}\) for \(x \neq 3\). (a) Determine the inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\). (b) State the domain and range of \(f^{-1}(x)\).
question.ar: ليكن \(f(x) = \dfrac{2x + 1}{x - 3}\) for \(x \neq 3\). (a) حدّد inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\). (b) State the domain and range of \(f^{-1}(x)\).

solution.en:
(a) Find the inverse function: Set \(y = \dfrac{2x + 1}{x - 3}\). Swap \(x\) and \(y\): \[ x = \dfrac{2y + 1}{y - 3} \implies x(y - 3) = 2y + 1 \implies xy - 3x = 2y + 1. \] Group \(y\) terms: \[ xy - 2y = 3x + 1 \implies y(x - 2) = 3x + 1 \implies \mathbf{f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{3x + 1}{x - 2}}. \]

(b) Domain and Range: The denominator of \(f^{-1}(x)\) cannot be zero, so the domain is \(\mathbf{(-\infty, 2) \cup (2, \infty)}\) (all \(x eq 2\)). The range of \(f^{-1}\) equals the domain of \(f\), which is \(\mathbf{(-\infty, 3) \cup (3, \infty)}\) (all \(y eq 3\)).

question.en: Solve the exponential equation \(3^{2x - 1} = 5^{x + 2}\) for \(x\) in terms of natural logarithms.
question.ar: حل the exponential equation \(3^{2x - 1} = 5^{x + 2}\) for \(x\) in terms of natural logarithms.

solution.en:
Step 1: Take the natural logarithm of both sides: \[ \ln(3^{2x - 1}) = \ln(5^{x + 2}) \implies (2x - 1)\ln(3) = (x + 2)\ln(5). \]

Step 2: Expand and group all terms containing \(x\): \[ 2x\ln(3) - \ln(3) = x\ln(5) + 2\ln(5) \implies x[2\ln(3) - \ln(5)] = 2\ln(5) + \ln(3). \]

Step 3: Solve for \(x\): \[ x = \mathbf{\frac{2\ln(5) + \ln(3)}{2\ln(3) - \ln(5)}} = \mathbf{\frac{\ln(75)}{\ln(9/5)}} \approx 7.37. \]

question.en: The function \(f(x) = \dfrac{4x - 7}{2x + 8}\) has horizontal asymptote \(y = H\) and vertical asymptote \(x = V\). Determine the value of \(H + V\).
question.ar: The function \(f(x) = \dfrac{4x - 7}{2x + 8}\) has horizontal asymptote \(y = H\) and vertical asymptote \(x = V\). حدّد value of \(H + V\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Find horizontal asymptote \(y = H\): Since degrees of numerator and denominator are both 1, the horizontal asymptote is the ratio of leading coefficients: \[ H = \frac{4}{2} = 2. \]

Step 2: Find vertical asymptote \(x = V\): Set denominator to zero: \[ 2x + 8 = 0 \implies 2x = -8 \implies V = -4. \]

Step 3: Compute sum: \[ H + V = 2 + (-4) = \mathbf{-2}. \]

question.en: Given the function \( f(x) = 2x + 3 \). What is the value of \( f^{-1}(7) \)?
question.ar: Given the function \( f(x) = 2x + 3 \). ما قيمة \( f^{-1}(7) \)?

hints.en: Let \( y = f(x) \). Then \( y = 2x + 3 \). To find the inverse function \( f^{-1}(y) \), we swap \( x \) and \( y \) and solve for \( y \).
hints.ar: ليكن \( y = f(x) \). Then \( y = 2x + 3 \). To أوجد inverse function \( f^{-1}(y) \), we swap \( x \) and \( y \) and أوجد قيمة \( y \).

hints.en: So, \( x = 2y + 3 \). Subtract 3 from both sides: \( x - 3 = 2y \). Divide by 2: \( y = \frac{x - 3}{2} \). Thus, \( f^{-1}(x) = \frac{x - 3}{2} \).

hints.en: We need to find \(f^{-1}(7)\). Substitute \(x = 7\) into the inverse function: \(f^{-1}(7) = \frac{7 - 3}{2}\).
hints.ar: We need to أوجد \(f^{-1}(7)\). عوّض \(x = 7\) into the inverse function: \(f^{-1}(7) = \frac{7 - 3}{2}\).

solution.en:
Let \( y = f(x) \). Then \( y = 2x + 3 \). To find the inverse function \( f^{-1}(y) \), we swap \( x \) and \( y \) and solve for \( y \).
So, \( x = 2y + 3 \).
Subtract 3 from both sides: \( x - 3 = 2y \).
Divide by 2: \( y = \frac{x - 3}{2} \).

We need to find \( f^{-1}(7) \). Substitute \( x = 7 \) into the inverse function:
\( f^{-1}(7) = \frac{7 - 3}{2} = \frac{4}{2} = 2 \).
